uncited: This family extends 3D Gaussian Splatting to support semantic understanding and natural language queries by integrating feature fields or semantic codes into the Gaussian primitives .
It solves the limitation of standard 3DGS, which only renders photometric color, by enabling open-vocabulary object localization and segmentation .
It differs from sibling optimization techniques (e.g., [TurboGS](15697-turbogs.md)) by focusing on the semantic attribute representation rather than rendering speed or geometry constraints alone.

All methods in this family augment the standard 3D Gaussian parameter set $\Theta_i = \{x_i, q_i, s_i, \alpha_i, c_i\}$ with a semantic attribute $f_i$ or $\beta_i$ [15902-feature-3d-gaussian-splatting.md, 15436-fast-splat.md].
where $F_s$ is the rendered semantic feature, $\alpha_i$ is opacity, and $T_i$ is transmittance [15902-feature-3d-gaussian-splatting.md].

Training involves a joint loss function combining photometric reconstruction (L1/SSIM) and a semantic distillation or classification loss [15436-fast-splat.md, 15902-feature-3d-gaussian-splatting.md].
Originating from the need to add semantic understanding to explicit 3D representations, these methods build on [3D Gaussian Splatting](9128-3d-gaussian-splatting-implementation-details.md).
LangSplat adapts the training loop to include language losses [12438-langsplat-training-procedure.md].
FAST-Splat introduces semantic codes and hash-tables for open-set detection [15436-fast-splat.md].
Feature 3DGS focuses on distilling 2D foundation model features into 3D Gaussians [15902-feature-3d-gaussian-splatting.md].
